item.title: Salabiau earns All Blacks Sevens call-up after impressive NPC season
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 18/11/2026 Fiji-born Waikato winger Waisake Salabiau has been named in the 22-member All Blacks Sevens squad for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS World 7s Series.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 18/11/2026

Fiji-born Waikato winger Waisake Salabiau has been named in the 22-member All Blacks Sevens squad for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS World 7s Series.

Salabiau had a breakout season for Waikato, showcasing his speed and footwork as he scored seven tries in nine NPC matches.

He will be joined by Akuila Rokolisoa and Kele Lasaqa.

Head coach Willie Rickards has named five uncapped players for this season, including Salabiau, Brayden Neilson, Grady Forbes, Nathan Salmon and Adam Morrison.

Rickards has also recalled experienced playmakers Joe Webber and Andrew Knewstubb after both players missed the 2026 sevens season.

Rob Rush and experienced campaigner Sione Molia will co-captain the All Blacks Sevens side.

The All Blacks will open their Dubai 7s campaign against the Fiji Airways Fiji men's national 7s side at 8.36pm next Saturday.

They will then face Spain at 11.39pm before meeting France at 4.22am on Sunday, 29th November.

The men's cup semi-finals will kick off at 10.06pm on Sunday, with the final scheduled for 4.11am on Monday, 30th November.

Fiji Airways National 7s teams present i-tatau ahead of Dubai campaign
item.description: The Fiji Airways Men’s and Women’s National 7s teams presented their i-tatau today as they prepare to depart for Dubai for their upcoming international campaigns. The National Men’s Basketball Team, along with the Boys’ and Girls’ Basketball teams, also presented their i-tatau ahead of their respective international commitments.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Airways Men’s and Women’s National 7s teams presented their i-tatau today as they prepare to depart for Dubai for their upcoming international campaigns.

The National Men’s Basketball Team, along with the Boys’ and Girls’ Basketball teams, also presented their i-tatau ahead of their respective international commitments.

Minister for Sports Jese Saukuru says as the National 7s teams and other sporting teams prepare to represent Fiji on the international stage, they carry with them the hopes and pride of the nation.

He reminds the delegations that they are ambassadors of the country and contribute to the nation’s economic growth through their hard work and by promoting Fiji as a tourism destination.

Saukuru wishes all the athletes the very best as they embark on their respective campaigns.

The Dubai 7s tournament will be held next Saturday to Sunday.

Fiji Men's will face New Zealand in their first pool match on Saturday at 8.36pm before taking on France at 11.17pm.

They will then face Spain in their final pool match at 4am on Sunday.

Fiji Women's will face Canada at 6.44pm on Saturday before taking on Japan at 9.44pm.

They will then play New Zealand at 2.52am.
